problems: The arch cylinder overlaps the slab box and their front faces both sit at y = -0.08. The overlapping faces flicker against each other and leave a large glassy disc across the middle of the stone, and the chip warp distorts the cylinder's flat end faces, so the stone doesn't read as one solid gravestone. Build the slab as one warped piece instead.
The cross's upright and crossbar share the same front face, which leaves a black square where they cross. Move the crossbar slightly forward.
The light gray stone renders almost white, and the pale ledge is nearly the same colour, so the stone doesn't stand out from it. Use a darker gray for the stone and a warmer, darker ledge.
The moss patch on top of the arch is mostly hidden inside the stone. Raise it so it sits on the curved top.

The cross reads as a 'T': the crossbar sits almost at the top of the upright, which shows only a sliver above it, and the two bars stand at different depths. Lower the crossbar so the upright clearly continues above it, and put both bars in one plane.
The stone renders nearly white, not light gray, on both the slab and the plinth. Darken the stone hexes so the card reads as gray stone.

The lower-left moss is a tall green column with a puddle spreading from its foot. It reads as slime or goo, not moss. Make it a low, lumpy patch pressed flat against the front face that wraps the corner and creeps a little onto the plinth, in a less neon green.
The top-left moss sits behind the arch and barely shows from the camera. Bring it onto the arch's front edge and top so it reads.
